title: i want to talk about "when i am dead and white" (1967), cause i doubt anyone will hear about it otherwise

commenti.body:
Yugoslavian black wave is one of the many similar worldwide movements of that time, but maybe also one of the most interesting (alongside Brazilian "Cinema Novo")

I'd also recommend "a man is not a bird" it's a lesser known black-wave film which I really liked.

> I'd also recommend "a man is not a bird" it's a lesser known yugo black-wave film, which I really liked (it's on YouTube).

I remember liking that one a lot, too. Thanks for reminding me; maybe I'll rewatch it.

Haven’t explored yet the Yugoslav new wave, but there were similar movements in many other smaller movie countries in the 50’s, 60’s and 70’s;

The Iranian wave was very inspired https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_New_Wave - Forugh Farrokhzad was an iconoclast -  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forugh_Farrokhzad

There was a new wave in Egypt, in the 50-6’s

South America has movements all over, Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Chile…

And of course Japan…
Was Yousef Chahine considered a part of the movement in Egypt? I loved some of his stuff from the 60es
Yes, he was one of them, Cairo station is a gem
